observation.visible_scene: A wide, elevated view of a city skyline under a thick, uniform gray overcast sky. In the foreground are red-tiled rooftops and chimneys; mid-ground shows apartment blocks, a tall brick smokestack, and on the right two red construction cranes over a building under construction. The horizon is hazy, with a pale yellowish band of light at the far left. The camera is fixed throughout (buildings, cranes and rooftops hold identical frame positions).
visible_changes: A dark, blurry, roughly circular spot (consistent with an out-of-focus water droplet or smudge on the lens) appears in the left-central sky around frame 14 and persists to the end, only slightly changing shape.
From about frame 34 onward, an additional blurry dark patch with a downward vertical streak appears in the center-right/lower area, also consistent with a droplet on the lens.
Overall scene contrast gradually decreases: the city skyline and distant horizon become progressively hazier and more washed out across the clip.
The pale yellowish glow at the left horizon dims and blends into the surrounding gray, reducing the brightness difference between sky and horizon.
Cloud cover remains heavy and gray the whole time, with only subtle shifts in cloud texture and no large-scale cloud translation detectable against the static camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the dark spots are lens droplets (rain/mist) or actual low clouds cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
The cause of the increasing haze (fog, rain, or camera auto-exposure/white-balance drift) is not determinable.
What precedes the first frame and what follows the last frame is unseen; the droplet spots and the haze trend may continue beyond the excerpt.
uncertain_details: Exact identity of the blurry dark blobs (lens artifact vs. atmospheric feature).
Whether any slow cloud drift exists or the sky texture change is purely due to lighting/haze.
Direction and magnitude of the haze increase are gradual and partly ambiguous.
